title: rubus macrophyllus subsp. eglandulosus
intro: Rubus macrophyllus subsp. eglandulosus, commonly known as Korean black raspberry, is a plant species in the rose family (Rosaceae) that is native to East Asia. This plant has been traditionally used in medicine due to its health benefits, including antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and anti-cancer properties, which may help protect against chronic diseases such as heart disease and certain types of cancer. The therapeutic actions of Korean black raspberry include antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and antimicrobial activities, which may help to soothe and protect the skin, reduce inflammation, and prevent infections. The bioactive constituents of this plant include flavonoids, anthocyanins, and phenolic acids, which are responsible for its medicinal properties and have been shown to have potential health benefits.
